sourceInformation.perspective: Elevated third-person with an orbit camera
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPU, Rapier 0.19.3, Web Audio, Gamepad API, PeerJS 1.5.5, AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded, ink-outlined storybook night; warm windows, redwoods, and fireflies
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip, and keyframe tracks; procedural scene effects
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-synthesized music, sound effects, and Animalese-style gibberish voices. Music defaults to 10%.
sourceInformation.online: 1–4 player shared-world co-op: AI Hub sessions; standalone WebRTC rooms with PeerJS signaling and BroadcastChannel local transport
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium 153 with software WebGPU; full Rapier playthrough, standard gamepad stub, touch profile, synthesized waveform checks, two-page co-op, and four official Hub harness scenarios. Screenshots only for visual review, using the WebGL diagnostic backend. Physical devices and remote internet/NAT traversal: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: No internet research. Native model knowledge; only the user-linked AI Hub integration files and pinned dependency packages were downloaded.

testingFeedback: 11 distinct issues found through scripted tests, visual checks, and code review; all fixed. See issue-log.json in the development folder.
3 critical issues: corrupted inline packaging, ending-screen synchronization, and Hub startup timing.
The complete scripted playthrough using real Rapier movement; it exposed an inaccessible flower and verified the bridge, transmitter, six flight rings, rescues, saves, and ending.
Direct headless WebGPU screenshots were least helpful: they could stall despite a working simulation. GPU state checks and WebGL diagnostic captures were more useful.
engineFeedback: The scene graph, TSL material nodes, and native AnimationMixer clips made procedural characters, bicycles, and a coherent ink-outlined world practical.
Yes. I initially placed the Hub handshake after graphics initialization and used browser flags that produced a lost WebGPU device. Separate protocol and minimal GPU checks identified both.
The adventure state machine, visibility and bond systems, controller-first interface, synthesized soundscape, and authoritative co-op with latched input edges.
Coordinating asynchronous WebGPU startup, shader preparation, scene visibility, and multiple copies while meeting the Hub readiness barrier.
none; the engine libraries are unmodified. Custom materials, geometry, animation clips, and gameplay are application code.
A standard WebGPU cel-lighting material and an outline pass that cooperate with shadows and camera cutaways.
promptFeedback: The emotional source, code-only audio, and requirement for a complete controller-first adventure gave the game a strong identity.
The no-internet-research instruction coexists with a required online integration link; I treated that link as implementation documentation, not source research.
Combining a complete adventure, authoritative four-player co-op, portable single-file packaging, and readable TV, keyboard, and touch controls.
Explicitly exempt the required integration documentation and dependency downloads from the research restriction.

aiHub.name: E.T. the Extra-Trusting
aiHub.tagline: The way home begins with a friend.
aiHub.description: Pedal through a moonlit suburb with a small stranded visitor in your basket. Borrow transmitter parts, hide from searchlights, restore the woods, and follow a thread of starlight home, alone or with up to three friends.
aiHub.controls: Left stick/WASD ride; right stick/right-drag camera; ×/E help; □/Q glow; ○/F candy; R2/Space boost; L2/Shift hush; △/Tab map; Options/Esc pause. Touch: left-thumb slide, right tap help, double-tap glow.
